clue.text: Stop being a TV viewer's plaything

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: to jack in (give up) the box (the television)
second meaning: a toy figure on a spring that pops out of a box

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stop being a mere toy of the television.
explanation.walkthrough: To jack in is British slang for to quit, and the box is the television, so the phrase literally means giving up the telly. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a children's toy in which a puppet springs out when the lid opens.

clue.text: After a short time, get hold of small items put in the post

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment
to bag something is to secure it
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A quick errand: grab the little packets and send them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just signals the order: the short time comes first, then the getting hold, then small.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiffy bags are padded envelopes, a trademark name for the packets people send by mail.

clue.text: Ferry operator retaining games supervisor

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Charon ferries the dead across the Styx in Greek myth
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A boat operator has a referee aboard to oversee some games.
explanation.walkthrough: Games is not a sports fixture here but school PE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an older person who supervises and accompanies the young, especially at social occasions.

clue.text: Playmaker's chronic complaint over Everton's wingers

parts.note: irritable bowel syndrome, a long-term condition

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the two outside letters of the word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of Everton

explanation.surface: A football midfielder has a persistent grumble about Everton's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' looks like football jargon but means a maker of plays. In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist, wrote plays such as A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: European punching body part — nose gets swollen

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so this letter is driven in between the other pieces

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach
E is the abbreviation for European
a dog's nose is its sense of smell, its scent

explanation.surface: A brawl abroad: someone is punched and their nose puffs up.
explanation.walkthrough: The European letter is punched in between the body part and the nose's sense, not into a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumescent is a formal word for swelling or swollen, often of body tissue.

clue.text: For the radio engineer, something beautiful to behold

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so a word is chosen for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Gustave Eiffel was the engineer behind the Paris tower

explanation.surface: A broadcast tribute calling some engineer's work a lovely sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineer is a particular one, Gustave Eiffel, whose surname is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is informal for an attractive sight, something well worth looking at.

clue.text: Excerpt from Antonioni's domestic tear-jerker?

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage taken out of a larger work, so the letters lie inside the next word

parts.note: the letters run through the middle of the director's name

explanation.surface: A scene from an Antonioni film set at home that makes viewers weep.
explanation.walkthrough: Tear-jerker suggests a weepy film, but here it is a kitchen vegetable that makes your eyes run when chopped; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting an onion releases a vapour that makes the eyes water, a household cause of tears.

clue.text: Fans of the sauce really tucking into sauces

indicators.note: tucking into food puts it inside you, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: dips are sauces for dunking
so as an intensifier, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: Condiment enthusiasts get stuck into their sauces with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sauce' is slang for alcohol, so the fans are drinkers, not lovers of ketchup.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso is short for dipsomaniac, an informal word for a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Agent displaying the odds of Burberry receiving fine

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the second piece is placed inside the first
odds here means the odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of Burberry
OK means all right, fine

explanation.surface: A sales agent shows the betting odds on the fashion house Burberry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds' suggests betting, but it picks the odd letters. Burberry is a British luxury clothing brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent who arranges deals for others, such as buying shares or insurance.

clue.text: Characters inspired by Benjamin Franklin later on

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the characters are drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: Fictional characters later in history modelled on Benjamin Franklin.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra is Latin for below, used in documents to point to a passage further on.
explanation.definitionFit: In footnotes and references, 'see infra' directs the reader to something below, that is later in the text.

clue.text: Department stores priest runs for one who waits

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so the department holds the priest

parts.note: the Somme is a French administrative department
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A shop's staff: department stores employ a priest who handles running errands.
explanation.walkthrough: Department means a French region, not part of a shop. SOMM(ELI)E is followed by R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine waiter in a restaurant, someone who waits at table serving wine.

clue.text: Spooner's child spotted miso ingredient

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: a child is a boy, and spotted means seen

explanation.surface: A youngster was seen with a miso ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and S of BOY SEEN gives SOY BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a Japanese paste made by fermenting soybeans with salt and koji.

clue.text: Satellite broadcaster mostly welcoming new input

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the remaining piece goes inside
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A satellite TV company mostly accepts fresh suggestions from viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY loses its last letter to give SK, which then takes in the rearranged INPUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957, was the first artificial satellite to orbit the Earth.

clue.text: Peril in the deep sewer, working inside it

indicators.note: inside it tells us to place one piece within the earlier word

parts.note: a sewer here is one who sews, a seamster
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: A sewer worker is in danger deep underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewer is not a drain but someone who sews, and 'it' points back to that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea monsters are legendary creatures said to menace sailors in the ocean depths.

clue.text: Opening of supermarket destroys clothes shop, creating workforce issue

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: first letter of supermarket
to kill is to destroy
Gap is a chain of clothing stores

explanation.surface: A new supermarket drives a high-street clothes shop out of business, leaving staff problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A skills gap is a shortage of trained workers able to do the jobs employers need doing.

clue.text: Say Ivan Toney's shots always rebound? Only the headers

indicators.note: headers are the tops of things, so only the first letter of each word counts

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A complaint that striker Ivan Toney's efforts keep bouncing back, scoring only with headers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan Toney is an English footballer, and headers suits the football scene; the Ivan wanted is Ivan the Terrible, the first Russian ruler to take this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia is an example of a tsar, an emperor of Russia, hence 'say' as in 'for example'.

clue.text: Shanty about upright character joining navy salt?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a sea shanty is a sea song
the letter I is a single upright stroke
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A sailor's song about an upstanding character who joins the navy as an old salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a sailor but is the condiment; the question mark marks it as an example. SEA SON(I N)G.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is an example of seasoning, any flavouring added to food.

clue.text: Grand artist and I squabble about muralist's works

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the last two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A great painter and I argue about the merits of a muralist's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns round the I and the squabble together, not just one of them. RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is writing or pictures painted on walls in public places, the work of a street muralist.

clue.text: Blunder? If so, bumbler becomes humbler

wordplay.note: changing bumbler to humbler means swapping one letter for another

explanation.surface: A clumsy person's mistake might make them more modest.
explanation.walkthrough: The only difference between bumbler and humbler is that B turns into H, which the clue states as B IS H. Bish is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is informal British slang for a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: What's spent on Wall Street banks in large-scale collapse

parts.note: buck is American slang for a dollar

indicators.note: banks are the edges of a river, so only the outside letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of large-scale

explanation.surface: Wall Street banks bring about a huge financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the financial institutions, but it means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to give way or crumple under pressure, as a structure or a person may.

clue.text: Ex-president requires hand with task to perform

parts.note: mitt is informal for a hand
an errand is a small job to carry out

explanation.surface: A former head of state needs help with a job.
explanation.definitionFit: François Mitterrand was President of France from 1981 to 1995.

clue.text: Slag off Guardian setter, turning on a Guardian setter

indicators.note: turning round means the setter's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Fed is a pseudonym used by a Guardian crossword setter
taken as written
a setter often refers to themselves in a clue as me; here the setter is a Guardian one

explanation.surface: One Guardian compiler disparages another, turning on a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is used twice: once for the setter Fed, reversed, and once for the clue's own setter, ME. 'On' means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is British slang for to criticise harshly, which matches defaming someone's reputation.

clue.text: Attack right back in box that's well defended

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece within the box

parts.note: a safe is a strong box

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A football full-back attacks down the right in a penalty box that is well defended.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Legislature's better current tax cut

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or better
I is the symbol for electric current
a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A parliament's improved current tax is being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, to top. TOLL loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitol in Washington is the building where the US Congress meets, the legislature's home.

clue.text: Reason why waiter may be annoyed around Spike

indicators.note: around means turned the other way, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.words: Reason why waiter may be annoyed
parts.note: a waiter left without a gratuity has reason to be cross

explanation.surface: A waiter grumbles about someone called Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike that climbers drive into rock to anchor a rope.

clue.text: Rocket leaves now starter for lunch, and swell cakes provided

indicators.note: to cake is to coat or encrust, so the outer pieces surround the inner one
a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of lunch
a swell or toff is a smart upper-class person
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A lunch menu: rocket salad, a starter, and fancy cakes are laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket is not the salad leaf but a spacecraft, and 'leaves' is a verb. The starter and the swell together form the outside layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment a rocket leaves the launch pad, the instant it departs.

clue.text: Fruit for Wilhelm I, cutting into large one

indicators.note: cutting into something goes inside it, so this piece sits within the others

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large
Roman numeral one
ich is German for I, as a German such as Wilhelm would say it

explanation.surface: Fruit offered to the German Kaiser, sliced into one big piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilhelm I looks like the Kaiser, but it means the word 'I' in Wilhelm's language.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichi is a variant spelling of lychee, a small sweet fruit from China.

clue.text: Wanting drive, hate travelling in empty Landcruiser with smoke coming from the back

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the emptied vehicle
coming from the back means read from the end towards the start
travelling means moving about, so these letters move into a new order
empty means the middle has been removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Landcruiser
taken as written
a cig is a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: An unmotivated driver of a hated, empty Land Cruiser with smoke pouring from the exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive here is energy, not motoring, and the Landcruiser is a vehicle emptied of its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic describes someone sluggish and lacking energy or motivation.

clue.text: Bit of hip old city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the large upper bone of the pelvis
second meaning: the Latin name for ancient Troy

explanation.surface: A trendy part of a historic town.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilium is the broad upper bone of the hip, and Ilium was the classical name for Troy.

clue.text: Join in revolution, deposing leader with initiative

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes the one at the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to enter is to join in
an uprising is a revolt

explanation.surface: Taking part in a revolt that topples the ruler shows real initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the revolution itself loses its leader: UPRISING drops its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising describes someone resourceful and showing initiative in new ventures.
